summary: A gauge with one score out of 100 for a design system, plus the checks that make it up, such as token usage, contrast and component reuse. Each check opens to show why it scored as it did, and a check marked fixable gets a Fix button that hands the job to the agent. When the fix lands, the check and the overall score update.
use: When an agent audits a design system or codebase and you want one number with the reasons behind it.
When some issues can be fixed by the agent with a click.
On a dashboard card that tracks quality over time.
features: The score sits large and bold inside the gauge, with a divider line between it and the checks below.
A half-circle gauge that fills to the score, which is the average of the checks unless you pass `score`.
Colours by score: green from 90, the accent colour from 80, red below 80.
A status line such as "Good, 2 checks need work" worked out from checks under 90, or your own `status`.
Pointing at a check, or moving the keyboard focus to it, swings the gauge to that check's score and puts its name and detail beside it; leaving the list swings it back to the overall score.
Each check is a row with a bar and its score; clicking it opens a line of `detail`.
A check with `fixable` gets a Fix button when `onFix` is set; if `onFix` returns a promise the button spins until it settles.
Score changes count to the new number, and the open rows can be controlled with `open` and `onOpenChange`.
a11y: The gauge has role="meter" with aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax 100, aria-valuenow set to the score and the title as its label.
Each check row is a button with aria-expanded, and its closed detail is inert and aria-hidden.
The Fix button sets aria-busy while the fix runs.
Number count-ups finish at once when the user prefers reduced motion.

faq.q: How do I let the agent fix a check?
faq.a: Set `fixable` on the check and pass `onFix`. Return a promise that resolves once the agent is done, then update that check's `score` and `detail` in `checks`. You may also want to clear `fixable` so the button goes away.

faq.q: How is the overall score worked out?
faq.a: By default it is the rounded average of all check scores. Pass `score` to show your own number instead, for example a weighted score.

faq.q: Can I open a check from outside the component?
faq.a: Yes. Control `open` with an array of check keys. A check's key is its `key`, or its `label` when no key is set.
